messages.subject: RE: TIme series plot with marginal distribution?
parts:
Hi Rick,

Is something like this what you are talking about?

library(ggplot2)


vplayout <- function(x, y)
viewport(layout.pos.row = x, layout.pos.col = y)

df <- data.frame(t = 1:1000, y = cumsum(rnorm(1000)))
rg <- range(df$y)
fn <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0, floor(x), ceiling(x))
rg <- sapply(rg, fn)

p <- qplot(x = t, y = y, data = df) + ylim(rg[1], rg[2])
q <- qplot(x = y, data = df) + coord_flip() + xlim(rg[1], rg[2])

x11(7, 3.5)
pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(1, 4)))
print(p, vp = vplayout(1, 1:3))
print(q, vp = vplayout(1, 4))

-----Mensaje original-----

messages.subject: Re: TIme series plot with marginal distribution?
parts:
Hi:

This is a slightly different take on Fernando's idea, but the essence is the same. Instead of using grid.layout(), define the sizes of the viewports manually and then populate them with the grobs (the actual graphs).

The second line of q removes the axis tick labels and the text label.
p <- qplot(x = t, y = y, data = df) + ylim(rg[1], rg[2])

q <- qplot(x = y, data = df) + coord_flip() + xlim(rg[1], rg[2]) +
   opts(axis.text.y = theme_blank()) + xlab('')

I don't know how to control the spacing at the margins of the plot in ggplot2, but tried to mitigate the problem somewhat by overlapping the viewports slightly. This is about as close as I could get without distorting one plot or the other.

Define the size and centers of the viewports:
vp1 <- viewport(width = 0.8, height = 1, x = 0.4, y = 0.5)
vp2 <- viewport(width = 0.25, height = 1, x = 0.875, y = 0.5)

# Open the graphics device:
x11(7, 3.5)
print(q, vp = vp2)
print(p, vp = vp1)

# dev.off()

I don't know if that's close enough for your needs, but if not, perhaps someone can embellish the code to get the graphs closer.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: TIme series plot with marginal distribution?
parts:
Hi Rick and Fernando:

Thanks for the compliments; much appreciated :)  I played a little more, blanking out plot.background(), and I think we are pretty close...how about this?

df <- data.frame(t = 1:1000, y = cumsum(rnorm(1000)))
rg <- range(df$y)
fn <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0, floor(x), ceiling(x))
rg <- sapply(rg, fn)

p <- qplot(x = t, y = y, data = df) + ylim(rg[1], rg[2])

q <- qplot(x = y, data = df) + coord_flip() + xlim(rg[1], rg[2]) +
           opts(axis.text.y = theme_blank()) + xlab('')

# strip off the plot backgrounds
p2 <- p + opts(plot.background = theme_blank())   
q2 <- q + opts(plot.background = theme_blank())
vp2 <- viewport(width = 0.25, height = 1, x = 0.875, y = 0.5)

vp3 <- viewport(width = 0.85, height = 1, x = 0.425, y = 0.5)   # a little wider than before

x11(7, 3.5)
print(q2, vp = vp2)
print(p2, vp = vp3)
# dev.off()

If you look *really* closely, you'll see that the axis ticks of the histogram still match that of the time plot.

Fernando, do you have an example to illustrate the use of negative margins to pull together 2 or more plots? I'd be interested in seeing that.

HTH,
Dennis

Hi Dennis,

 

Thanks for the further improved plot. I put an example of using negative axis margins bellow, nevertheless I think your code is more elegant.

Best regards,

fernando

 

p <- q <- qplot(1, 1) + opts(plot.background = theme_blank())

q <- q + opts(plot.margin = unit(c(1, 3, 0.5, -2.5), "lines")) # left margin negative compensated with a larger the right margin to maintain the proportions of the plot

 

grid.newpage()

pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(1, 2)))

print(p, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 1))

print(q, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 2))

# strip off the plot backgrounds
p2 <- p + opts(plot.background = theme_blank())   
q2 <- q + opts(plot.background = theme_blank())

vp2 <- viewport(width = 0.25, height = 1, x = 0.875, y = 0.5)
vp3 <- viewport(width = 0.85, height = 1, x = 0.425, y = 0.5)   # a little wider than before

x11(7, 3.5)
print(q2, vp = vp2)
print(p2, vp = vp3)
# dev.off()

If you look *really* closely, you'll see that the axis ticks of the histogram still match that of the time plot.
